decision: Cloud persistence backend for the first owner-only demo
decision_limits: No comparative workload measurements available. The judge identifies a suitable implementation slice only. It cannot establish deployed security or budget compliance.

evidence.claim: Generation-match preconditions enable conditional overwrite and generation zero allows creation only when no live object exists.
Cloud Storage policy can prevent overwrite/deletion before retention and can be locked. Working storage test does not authorize an irreversible lock.
Cloud Storage supports prefix and age scoped deletion; lifecycle execution is asynchronous.
Firestore provides transactions for concurrent writes. The option still needs a separate immutable audit path.

flip_conditions: If measured object latency, conflict frequency, or operating cost fails the owner demo budget, test a transactional Firestore state adapter against the same workload.

options.name: Cloud Storage for preferences with generation checks, append-only audit and lifecycle-managed telemetry
Firestore transactions for preferences and telemetry, with Cloud Storage for append-only audit

priorities.P2: Preserve concurrent preference updates and bounded telemetry
priorities.P3: Implementation and operating cost for the owner demo

requirements.text: Lets do durable memory and audit storage next. Test that the data survives a restart and retention works. Keep it owner-only until I test it and approve invites.
Repository operating directives require write-once retention for privileged audit and least-privilege runtime identity.
Keep preference writes merge-safe across instances. Use a proposed 30-day audit and 7-day telemetry retention, subject to review before provisioning. Local SQLite stays for local callers.
Actual end-to-end GCP costs, cloud permissions, and measured API latency for this application.

smallest_separating_test: Under the same test identities, run concurrent independent-field updates and a fresh-process recall with both backends and measure write latency, request cost, and correctness. Use the same append-only audit and retention controls.
